historical_record.description: North Beach Place, a public housing project designed in 1941-1942 by Henry Gutterson and Ernest Born, with landscape by Thomas Church and structural engineering by August V. Saph, opened its first units; delayed by the war, it was built in 1950-1952 by Leo Epp, Inc. on two blocks the city had taken by eminent domain, whose warehouses, flats and the Cable Car Restaurant were demolished in March and April 1950.

When the Housing Authority refused three qualified African-American families at North Beach Place under its "neighborhood pattern" segregation policy, the NAACP sued, and a Superior Court judge ruled the policy unconstitutional; the State District Court of Appeal upheld the ruling in August 1953 and the State Supreme Court in October 1953.

Demolition of the 1952 North Beach Place began on the east block in December 2001 and was finished on the west block in January 2003, for a HOPE VI rebuilding by BRIDGE Housing, the John Stewart Company and Em Johnson Interest.
